note: Work: 16. The Miscellaneous Provisions (Minimum Age for Admission to Employment) Act, 2007 (No. 3 of 2007, assented 26 February 2007, the gazette text the Ministry of Finance publishes) s. 2: subject to the Act, a person under sixteen shall not be admitted to employment, and the age governs 'child' and 'young person' in every other written law; it replaced the Children Act's s. 91 (under 16 not to work in any public or private undertaking except a family one, with school and training exceptions from 14). Performers: barred, the reading being that the 2007 Act has no exception for young performers. The Children Act, 2012 (No. 12 of 2012), which repealed and replaced Chap. 46:01, wasn't read, so whether it licenses child performances is unknown. Majority: 18. Age of Majority Act, Chap. 46:06 (Act 28 of 1973, in force 15 November 1973; the Ministry of the Attorney General's unofficial version updated to 31 December 2016, found by rendering laws.gov.tt's title search): a person attains full age at eighteen instead of twenty-one. Service: none. Defence Act, Chap. 14:01 (same edition) s. 19: a recruiting officer enlists a person offering to enlist who understands the notice and wishes to be enlisted.

sources.title: Ministry of Finance (Trinidad and Tobago): Miscellaneous Provisions (Minimum Age for Admission to Employment) Act, 2007 (Act No. 3 of 2007)
sources.said: [Assented to 26th February, 2007] ... Subject to this Act, a person under the age of ... sixteen shall not be admitted to employment.
